They are only upstream 2024.1 and 2024.2 and are tagged "Related-Bug", so it is unclear that the full fix is available for the target series. The tempest-plugin test job that closes the bug is a separate repository.

blockers.summary: Regression mentioned: "…ser-facing benefit? You note that this regressed in OpenSSL 3.0.14; is is possible to link the patch that was responsible for th…" (whershberger)

No SRU upload exists for resolute, the only affected release. The fix is only in the development release tenacious, and the stonking debdiff is of doubtful value because OpenSSL 4 has no engines and the second patch is a no-op there. The reviewer asked for a PPA build and the request is unanswered.

The reviewer flagged the packaging as a blocker: 'Origin: backport' should be 'Origin: upstream'. Patch ordering in d/p/series and use of full commit hashes were also raised. There is no evidence these were fixed for the resolute upload.

The test plan reproducer fails in the reviewer's environment: tpm2-abrmd never becomes ready on resolute, and on stonking engine_pkcs11 is missing. The bug has not been reproduced or verified independently. The test plan also lacks an apt install line listing the dependencies.

The SRU description does not say the bug affects only resolute because OpenSSL 4 has no engine support. It does not link the OpenSSL 3.0.14 change that caused the regression, so Noble and Jammy cannot be ruled out, and it does not describe the stonking regression check.

A user reported that after the engine loads a TPM key once, libtss2-esys cannot create RSA keys in the same process (EVP_PKEY_fromdata_init returns -2), so re-authentication may fail. The user later said this was an unverified LLM hypothesis, so a possible residual or regression issue has not been ruled out.

The 1.9.1-0.1ubuntu4 build links libcrypto.so.4 and cannot be installed on 26.04. The resolute backport must be built against OpenSSL 3.5.5 without the openssl4 compat patch, and this has not been shown in a PPA or proposed build.

comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html

bugs.title: rpivid rejects HEVC decode requests unless SPS/PPS controls are sent again

blockers.summary: No patch, kernel git thread or merge proposal is linked or discussed. The upstream fix is not in rpi-6.8.y, so Noble needs a backport or SAUCE patch, and a reviewer cannot confirm one exists or applies cleanly to linux-raspi 6.8.

The test plan needs a source-built GStreamer 1.26.11, because Noble's packaged 1.24.2 has no v4l2slh265dec on this device. The verification is therefore hard to reproduce and does not use archive software, and the plan gives no build or install steps.

The regression analysis is thin. Making SPS/PPS optional moves the failure from queue time to frame setup ("SPS never set" with an errored buffer), and the test plan does not exercise that path or check that streams that already worked still decode.

No comments show anyone has tested the patched kernel, so the fix is unverified. The bug was reproduced only on a Pi 5 with kernel 6.8.0-1065, and the fix is untested on other raspi variants or other affected series.
